precepts.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Here am I; send me. That is the mindset of a leader, the same as David asking where Goliath was while everyone else cried about the situation.
precepts.point: The first mark of a leader's mindset: he believes he can get the job done. When an issue arises you do not run; you raise your hand, volunteer, and find the solution.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.text: My lips shall utter knowledge clearly: the laws of God are clear to the righteous, so the water is clear as crystal.
precepts.point: The pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, is the word of God.

precepts.text: God speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and seals the instruction of men.
precepts.point: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done unto him? “For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not. In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction”.

The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night. Noah awoke from his wine and knew, because the Lord told him while deep sleep was upon him.

precepts.text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, He openeth the ears of men and sealeth their instruction.
precepts.point: When the sun went down a deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell on Abram: he was about to receive a vision of future prophecy. The Most High speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret to His servants the prophets.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
Abram had divided the heifer, the goat and the ram, and driven the fowls from the carcases; he was offering sacrifice. Then “when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him.” That deep sleep is how the Most High speaks.

Job shows it: “In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction.” The deep sleep that fell on Abram was the Most High opening his ears. He was about to receive a vision of future prophecy, the four hundred years of his seed.

precepts.text: Man's goings are of the Lord, so how can a man understand his own way; we must be mindful as we move through our day.
precepts.point: Many times we set out to do one thing and end up doing another, and later say the Lord was with me on this one, because he saved us from something terrible.

note.label: Job 33: Elihu Speaks God's Instruction to Man

precepts.why:
Elihu speaks on where the ways of man come from. In a dream, in a vision of the night, the Most High opens the ears of men and seals their instruction, “That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.” Proverbs says it plainly: “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

Everything we go through day in and day out, we may think we are doing what we want to do, but it is sealed in our minds what the Most High wants to happen in our lives. Many times we set out to do one thing and end up doing another, and later say the Lord was with me on this one, because he saved us from something terrible. That is him keeping back our soul from the pit and our life from perishing by the sword, so we must be mindful as we move through our day.

precepts.text: There is no man that sinneth not; when the captives in the land of their enemy repent, confess they have sinned and done perversely, and turn again with all their heart, God hears their prayer.
precepts.point: When we recognize we are in our transgressions and iniquity and we repent, then the Lord hears us.

note.label: Job 33: Elihu Speaks God's Instruction to Man

precepts.why:
Elihu says if any man says, “I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not”, God “will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.” Solomon prayed the same thing: “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness; And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul”, then “hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause”.

There is no man that sinneth not. When the captives in the land of their enemy repent, confess they have sinned and done perversely, and turn again with all their heart, God hears their prayer. When we recognize we are in our transgressions and iniquity and we repent, then the Lord hears us.

precepts.text: The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment; when we walk godly and according to the laws, the Lord has a way out for us.
precepts.point: When we recognize we are in our transgressions and iniquity and we repent, then the Lord hears us.

note.label: Job 33: Elihu Speaks God's Instruction to Man

precepts.why: “The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished”. When we walk godly and according to the laws, the Lord has a way out for us. That is the man who says I have sinned and perverted that which was right and it profited me not: God delivers his soul from going into the pit and his life sees the light, while the unjust are reserved unto the day of judgment to be punished.
